sections.markdown: AI is a broad label for computer systems performing tasks associated with intelligent behaviour. Machine learning is an approach in which behaviour is fitted from data rather than every rule being hand-written. Deep learning is a family of machine-learning methods using neural networks with multiple learned layers. These are overlapping categories, not three separate products. A system can use ordinary rules without learning from examples.

sections.markdown: Imagine sorting incoming messages. A fixed rule that flags a message when its subject contains a specified word uses no training data. A model fitted to labeled examples of spam and normal messages is machine learning. A multi-layer neural-network classifier is both deep learning and machine learning. Training adjusts learned parameters; inference applies the trained model to a new input. A correct-looking output alone does not establish how the system was built, and a learned model can still make mistakes.

sections.markdown:
Guided: a hand-written multiplication function does not become machine learning because it runs on a computer. Independent: a classifier is trained on past labeled messages using a multi-layer neural network. Which categories include it?

<details><summary>Explanation</summary>It is deep learning, which is within machine learning, used for an AI task. The evidence is the stated training method, not a brand name. This tells us nothing by itself about accuracy, fairness or reliability.</details>

Revision: distinguish task, learning method, training and inference; ask what data and evaluation support a claim. These offline scenarios do not require an API key or live model. Product-specific model features change; this lesson deliberately avoids claims about current model prices or capabilities.
